newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT-Chart strength seen in S&N vs Bass.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-Chart strength seen in S&N vs Bass.

text.p: + Recent chart breakout at 700p by Scottish & Newcastle shares indicates upward momentum for the stock and its share price should do better than that of Bass, technical analyst said.
* Since February, S&N has been outperforming Bass and this reinforces the case to switch out of Bass, they added.
Shares in the brewers, pubs and restaurants sector are a mixed bag but it presents an opportunity for switching between stocks, technical analysts said on Tuesday.

One such switch is between Bass and Scottish & Newcastle. Both stocks have suffered relative strength decline since the start of the year but Scottish & Newcastle looks better able to stop that rot, they added.
It's not a case that Scottish & Newcastle will power ahead but more that it will give a more robust performance than Bass over the medium-term.
By 0950 GMT, Bass shares were up 3p to 807-1/2p while Scottish & Newcastle was up 1/2p to 700-1/2p.

"Bass has been breaking down on relative strength (against the All-Share index) and chart breakout by Scottish & Newcastle looks positive (for the share price)," said Nick Glydon, technical analyst at Robert Fleming Securities.
But this positive trend has not been confirmed by the relative strength of Scottish & Newcastle which shows the stock has merely been moving in-line with the stock market for several weeks, he added.
Prior to the chart breakout, S&N had been shuffling sideways between 630p and 700p since February 1996 while the All-Share index had galloped ahead by 20 percent.
And according to Glydon, breakout from 700p in mid-May may be the first indication that Scottish & Newcastle has come out of its long-term consolidation phase.
In contrast, Bass shares have gained seven percent since February 1996 and over the past 12 months they have been restricted to a price range between 760p and 880p.
But with S&N marching higher over the past several weeks its relative strength over Bass now shows a positive trend.
This relative trend between the two stocks is expected to continue so that an opportunity now exists for switching out of Bass and into Scottish & Newcastle, said Glydon.
"Scottish & Newcastle is not overbought," he added.
